newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab press applauds "valiant knight" Chirac.
newsitem.headline: Arab press applauds "valiant knight" Chirac.

text.p: The Arab press on Wednesday hailed French President Jacques Chirac's visit to the Middle East, praising his efforts to seek a European role in the peace process and applauding his call for a Palestinian state.
"The courageous positions that Chirac adopted clearly take the side of truth and justice in the bitter conflict between Israel and the Arab states," said Egyptian government newspaper al-Ahram.

The Arab press was quick to find meaning in Chirac's scuffle on Tuesday in Arab East Jerusalem with overzealous Israeli security guards, whose heavy presence made it impossible for him to greet Palestinians.

"Because Chirac came to the region to urge Israel's rulers to adhere to the land-for-peace principle and the basis of the peace process, he was met with deliberate provocation by the Israeli leaders," the official Syrian daily Tishreen said.

Al-Dustour newspaper in Jordan, where Chirac will go later on Wednesday after a visit to the Palestinian-ruled Gaza Strip, said the incident showed the "intolerance and lack of vision" of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government.

During Chirac's visit to Jerusalem's Old City he turned frustrated at the tide of security guards around him, but when he snapped at them to leave -- asking if they wanted him to get on a plane and return to France -- they ignored him. Israel later apologised, saying it had been trying to protect him.

But there was no doubt that Israel was displeased with some of Chirac's statements, including the call he made in Syria at the weekend that Europe should have a role in the Middle East peace process as co-sponsor with the United States.
This was rejected by Israel before Chirac even arrived on Monday after two days in Syria, with Netanyahu saying it would probably not "be wise" to introduce "more cooks to the broth".

"The Israeli rejection of a European role is due to the fact that the Tel Aviv leaders could not blackmail Europe as they do with the U.S. That is why the Israelis deliberately placed obstacles against Chirac's mission," Tishreen said.

Chirac also told Israelis that their security could only be guaranteed by a Palestinian state, something Netanyahu opposed during his successful campaign to unseat Labour leader Shimon Peres in May elections.

"With the courage of a valiant knight, he took by storm the rejectionist positions of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. He told him, and all Israelis, on their own ground, that they must respect the fundamental elements in a peaceful settlement in the Middle East," Egypt's al-Akhbar daily said.
Iraq also fell behind Chirac, saying that he was a much better leader than predecessor Francois Mitterrand.

"The current visit by French President Jacques Chirac to Arab countries and the Zionist entity (Israel) reflects the new policy followed by France since Chirac assumed power," the official newspaper al-Thawra said.
